title: Words Spellable From a Letter Tray
statement:
You hold a tray of letter tiles, given as the string tray. You also get a list of words.

A word is spellable if you can lay it out using tiles from the tray, where each tile is used at most once inside that word. Every word is checked against the full tray on its own: tiles used for one word go back before the next word is checked.

Return the sum of the lengths of all spellable words.

examples.why: "bead", "bed" and "dab" fit (4 + 3 + 3). "babe" needs two b tiles and the tray has one.
"sun" (3) and "us" (2) fit. "nuns" needs two n tiles; the tray letters are reused per word, but never twice inside one word.
Containing every distinct letter is not enough: "zoo" needs two o tiles.

hints: Order of letters does not matter, only how many of each letter you have.
Count the tray letters once. For each word, count its letters and compare.
A word fits when, for every letter, the word needs no more copies than the tray has.

explain.intuition:
Spelling a word from tiles ignores order completely. All that matters is the count of each letter. So turn the tray into a count table once, then turn each word into a count table and check that no letter is needed more often than the tray has it.

With only 26 letters, a fixed array of 26 counters is the cheapest table, and comparing two of them costs constant time.
steps: Build have[26]: how many tiles of each letter the tray holds.
For each word, build need[26] the same way.
If need[c] ≤ have[c] for every letter, add the word's length to the answer.
pitfalls: Checking only that each letter of the word appears in the tray. That misses repeated letters, like "zoo" with one o tile.
Removing tiles from the tray permanently. Each word is checked against the full tray.

solutions.title: Use up tiles from a copy
solutions.idea: For each word, copy the tray into a list and delete one matching tile per letter. If a letter has no tile left, the word does not fit.

solutions.title: Letter counts
solutions.idea: Count the tray once. A word fits when its count of every letter is at most the tray's count.

followups: The tray is fixed and millions of words stream in. What would you precompute?
Return the longest spellable word instead, breaking ties alphabetically.
